newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia sees 1.65 bln rgt '97 trade deficit.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia sees 1.65 bln rgt '97 trade deficit.

text.p: Malaysia on Tuesday said its exports are expected to increase 7.5 percent this year, but imports will grow 8.0 percent leading to a 1997 trade deficit of 1.65 billion ringgit ($627.38 million).
In its 1996/97 annual report, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry projected total exports for 1997 at 211.44 billion ringgit against 196.69 billion last year.
Imports were estimated at 213.1 billion against 197.30 billion in 1996.
Malaysia recorded a 619 million ringgit deficit in 1996, a dramatic improvement from 9.4 billion ringgit in 1995.

International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz told a briefing on the report Malaysia could reach its 7.5 percent export growth target if the key electronics sector recovers strongly in the second half of the year.
Electrical and electronic goods and components accounted for 67.6 percent of Malaysia's manufactured exports in 1996 and has maintained that rate in the first five months of 1997, she said.
But the sector has been a double-edged sword, as far as the deficit is concerned, due to its high usage of imported components.
Total exports of electronic and electrical goods were 104.3 billion ringgit in 1996 but the sector also imported goods worth 104.7 billion ringgit, she said.
Malaysia would have to see a strong resurgence in its export performance in the second half to meet its 7.5 percent target.
The Statistics Department on Monday said in the first six months of 1997 exports rose by 1.8 billion ringgit, or 1.9 percent, to 98.4 billion ringgit from 96.6 billion in the first half of 1996.
By contrast, imports in the first half totalled 101.1 billion, up 3.9 billion, or four percent, from 97.2 billion in the same period last year.
The department said Malaysia posted a 2.8 billion ringgit trade deficit in June. It was the biggest monthly deficit in at least 17 years, analysts said.
The cumulative deficit for the first half of this year was 2.7 billion ringgit against 688 million ringgit in the same period last year.
A five percent depreciation of the ringgit this year should help boost Malaysia's flagging exports, analysts said.

"We expect exports to pick up in (second half 1997), backed by stronger electronics exports and the increased competitiveness of Malaysia with the ringgit depreciation," the Thong & KayHian research house said on Tuesday. "Our forecast for the full year trade deficit remains at 1.5 billion."
The ministry report said Malaysia in 1996 maintained its position as the world's 19th largest exporter and 17th largest importer.
Total investments were also off last year's robust performance, according to the report.

Malaysia has approved 5.41 billion ringgit in foreign investment in the first six months of 19997, Rafidah said. That compared with a total of 17.06 billion for all of 1996, according to the annual report.
Rafidah said Malaysia had approved 12.6 billion ringgit in total investments in the first six months of 1997, with 43 percent coming from foreign investors.
That compares with a total of 34.26 billion ringgit in approved investment projects for all of 1996. In 1995, total investment was 20.87 billion of which 9.1 billion came from foreign sources.
The bulk of foreign investment -- 9.2 billion ringgit or 54 percent of the total in 1996 -- was in the electrical and electronics sector.
($1=2.63 ringgit)
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
